prompt:
Render a high-fidelity desktop homepage UI mockup for FoodBridge, edge to edge at 1536 by 1024, crisp legible text, no browser frame or device. FoodBridge coordinates surplus food and waste collection in Sri Lanka. Donors, recipient organisations, recyclers, volunteers, and admins deserve equal visibility. The visitor's job is to understand the service and enter the right role. The visual world is a contemporary community wayfinding system: deep leaf-green information fields, clean white and pale mint grounds, sparing sunflower yellow for orientation. Broad humanist sans lettering, generous directional spacing, simple numbered destinations, restrained arrow signs; this is a usable website, not an illustrated street or poster. No fake numbers, testimonials, certifications, maps, current jobs, or impact claims.
Lead with a role-index concept at bolder scale. Navigation reads "FoodBridge.", "How it works", "Community impact", "Sign in". Five full-width typographic horizontal destination bands own the first screen, each with a quiet sequence number, generous role name and a precise action aligned at the far edge. Every role is legible without selecting a tab, scrolling a carousel, or hovering; do not hide four roles behind an active one. The compact introduction "Good food. Shared responsibility." and "Food sharing and waste collection in Sri Lanka." sits inside the same sign system rather than becoming a large generic hero above it. Use real role actions with equal prominence: "Donor — Share food or post waste"; "Recipient organisation — Register for review"; "Recycler — Register for review"; "Volunteer — Help with pickups"; "Admin — Sign in to manage". Each has a clear clickable arrow or action. Include the readable disclosure "Recipient and recycler browsing and claims are not available yet." Public admin signup must not appear.
Vary the white, mint and deep green fields with the discipline of one civic sign family, and one yellow orientation detail. No five separate floating cards or ornamental icon badges. The next section begins naturally at the lower edge with "Every handover needs a clear record", a narrow documentary photo of a food crate handover and a clear "View community impact" link. Preserve the dignity of people depicted; the image illustrates the work and proves no outcome.
